I also see that some patients don't have

Yeah, so transfusion medicine, I can tell you, it's one of those field that not many
people in healthcare may not know it as a speciality because, again, we are hidden in
The lab medicine, which is traditionally not a place where patients care is involved.
What is known about transfusion medicine is blood bank.
So we, the transfusion medicine specialists, specialize in transfusion, blood transfusion.
We oversee blood bank.
We make sure that, you know, the blood that comes out of the blood bank is compatible, it's safe.
And we also specialize in managing reaction after blood transfusion.
So we work with our colleagues that are all in the front line with the patient.
When things happen, then they get to call us.
The other aspect of transfusion medicine is what we call apheresis.
It's a procedure using a machine that looks like a diagnosis machine.
but it's a procedure that we can collect different blood components
either separately or together.
So we can select just red cell and take it out.
We can take out plasma.
We can take out granulose and all that.
These are all components of blood.
In addition to that, we can take out stem cells.
So the way it works is that patients get treated with a growth factor that stimulates the stem cell to come out.
They grow and then come out into circulation.
Then we use the aphoresis machine to collect it.
So we not only collect, we do therapy.
So there are patients that have, let's say, leukemia, and they have a lot of cells that even their blood is so thick, it doesn't flow well.
While we are the ones that come with our machine and take out those super excess number of white cells.
